deep.reconstruction:
Setting: H is a Hilbert space and the algebra is a semifinite von Neumann algebra with a normal faithful trace Tr. P is the set of projections. On the previous page, phi_A(t) is the generalized singular-value (rearrangement) function. For A >= 0 it is the decreasing rearrangement of the spectral distribution of A with respect to Tr; in modern notation it is mu_t(A). Prop. 1 there gives a Courant–Fischer min-max formula: phi_A(t+0) = inf_{Tr E < t} sup_{x in (1-E)H} (Ax,x). Its proof uses comparison of projections: if Tr E < Tr F then (1-E)H ∩ FH ≠ 0. Cor. 2 gives the ideal inequality mu(PAQ) <= ||P|| ||Q|| mu(A). Prop. 2 states mu(|A|) = mu(|A*|).

Top of this page: end of the proof of Prop. 2. Taking p-th powers, Tr (AA*)^p = Tr (A*A)^p for all p >= 1 (cyclicity of the trace, applied twice). So AA* and A*A have the same moments and hence the same distribution.

Main new object: Delta_t(A) := psi_{|A|}(t) = exp ∫_0^t log mu_s(A) ds. This is the 'truncated Fuglede–Kadison determinant', i.e. the continuous analogue of the product of the first k singular values s_1...s_k. Delta_E denotes the Fuglede–Kadison determinant in the reduced algebra E M E with trace Tr restricted.

Proposition (assuming the algebra is continuous, so projections of every trace exist):
(i) Delta_t(A) = sup_{Tr E < t} Delta_E(EAE) for A >= 0. This is the von Neumann-algebra analogue of Ky Fan's multiplicative maximum principle: prod_{j<=k} lambda_j(A) = max over k-dimensional P of det(PAP|PH).
(ii) Delta_t(1+|A|) = sup over B with Tr|B| < t and ||B|| <= 1 of Delta_E(E(1_E+BA)E). Here E is a support projection of B, and B can be taken positive if A >= 0. This is the analogue of the variational formula behind Weyl's inequality |det(1+K)| <= prod(1+s_j(K)).

Proof sketch (the inequality '<='):
- Put A' = EAE and B' = BA.
- By Cor. 2, mu(A') <= mu(A) and mu(B') <= ||B|| mu(A) <= mu(A). Hence Delta_t(A') <= Delta_t(A) and Delta_t(1+|B'|) <= Delta_t(E(1+|A|)E) <= Delta_t(1+|A|).
- In the reduced algebra with total trace Tr E, Delta_E(B) = exp ∫ log mu_B(s) ds = exp ∫_0^{Tr E} log mu_B(s) ds = Delta_{Tr E}(B) for B >= 0.
- Finally mu_{|1+B|}(s) <= mu_{1+|B|}(s) = 1 + mu_{|B|}(s), which gives |Delta(1+B)| <= Delta(1+|B|). This is the Fuglede–Kadison form of Weyl's determinant inequality.

Equality is obtained from spectral projections of A, via the spectral decomposition mentioned in the text.

Purpose: build a theory of multiplicative (Weyl/Horn/Lidskii-type) singular-value inequalities and of Fredholm determinants det(1+A) for Tr-trace-class operators in type II∞ algebras. This continues the rearrangement theory Grothendieck published in Sém. Bourbaki 1955, exp. 113.
errors: Formula (i) is false as written with 'Tr E < t' (and the later 'Delta_E B = Delta_t B si Tr E <= t' is false with '<='). Delta_E(EAE) equals exp ∫_0^{Tr E} log mu_s(EAE) ds, so passing to ∫_0^t is legitimate only if mu_s(A) >= 1 on (Tr E, t]. Counterexample: A = eps·1 with eps < 1 gives Delta_E(eps E) = eps^{Tr E}, whose supremum over Tr E < t tends to 1, while Delta_t(A) = eps^t. The condition must be Tr E = t; the hypothesis 'algebra continuous' presumably serves exactly to make such E exist. Formula (ii) is unaffected because 1+|A| >= 1.
In (ii) the role of E (a support projection of B, or a projection with Tr E < t) is left implicit, and the reverse inequality (attainment via spectral projections) is only gestured at.

ideas.what: Generalized singular-value function phi_{|A|}(t) for operators in a semifinite von Neumann algebra, with min-max characterization and mu(|A|) = mu(|A*|) via equality of moments Tr(AA*)^p = Tr(A*A)^p
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck 1955 (Bourbaki exp. 113); systematized by Fack 1982 and Fack–Kosaki 1986
ideas.where_published: Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace, Sém. Bourbaki 1955

ideas.what: Truncated Fuglede–Kadison determinant Delta_t(A) = exp ∫_0^t log mu_s(A) ds and its variational characterization as a sup of Fuglede–Kadison determinants of compressions EAE over projections of trace t
ideas.modern_name: Ky Fan multiplicative maximum principle in semifinite von Neumann algebras / truncated FK determinant
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fack–Kosaki 1986 (log-majorization ∫_0^t log mu_s); Fuglede–Kadison 1952 for the determinant; Haagerup–Schultz later use similar tools
ideas.where_published: possibly not in the Bourbaki exposé, which centres on convex (additive) rearrangement inequalities

ideas.what: Weyl-type determinant inequality |Delta(1+B)| <= Delta(1+|B|), with Delta_t(1+|A|) expressed as a sup of Delta_E(E(1+BA)E) over contractions B of trace < t
ideas.modern_name: Weyl inequality for Fredholm / Fuglede–Kadison determinants in type II
ideas.usually_credited_to: L. G. Brown (Lidskii's theorem in the type II case, 1983/86); de la Harpe–Skandalis 1984 for determinants associated with traces

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck combines his singular-value rearrangement functions with the Fuglede–Kadison determinant on reduced algebras EME. The aim is multiplicative Weyl/Ky Fan inequalities and a determinant det(1+A) for trace-class operators in II∞ algebras. This anticipates by about 30 years L. G. Brown's type-II Lidskii/Weyl theory and the Fack–Kosaki log-majorization ∫_0^t log mu_s, neither of which (to my knowledge) credits this multiplicative side to Grothendieck.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the multiplicative (determinantal) theory of generalized s-numbers, which underlies Brown measure and Haagerup–Schultz invariant subspace work. It also connects to Grothendieck's own 1956 Fredholm theory of nuclear operators.

missed.claim: The page builds variational formulas for the truncated FK determinant, apparently as a lemma towards Horn/Weyl product inequalities Delta_t(AB) <= Delta_t(A) Delta_t(B) and Delta_t(1+A+B) bounds in II∞. The thread stops here (the next page is essentially blank).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical; the results were later obtained independently.

deep.surprise_reason: The singular-value function itself is Grothendieck's published 1955 work. Combining it with Fuglede–Kadison determinants of compressions to get Ky Fan/Weyl multiplicative inequalities in type II (in 1953) predates Fack–Kosaki and L. G. Brown and seems unrecorded. However, the results were later found independently and the page contains an error in the first formula.
transcription_corrections: '(si E ...[?] continue)' likely means '(si l'algèbre est continue)' or similar: a continuity (non-atomic) hypothesis ensuring projections of any trace exist.
The marginal note under the second formula reads roughly '(on peut prendre B ∈ P si A ≥ 0)', i.e. B can be taken a projection or positive.
'Δ_t(1+|B'|) ≤ Δ_t E(1+|A|)E' is correct; the struck-out continuation is '≤ Δ_t(1+|A|)'.
In the bottom line, 'Δ_t(1+B) ≤ Δ(1+|B|)' should probably read with absolute value, |Δ(1+B)| ≤ Δ(1+|B|).
